items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: And we became friends. Actually I had known Chuck for a long time before I went into the service. But I started working that gig and we became friends. It was almost like family you know.

ctx.x: How did you get hooked up with the Jazz Brothers?

Chuck and Gap [Mangione]. Well after I came out of the service, you know I went into the Air Force and then I came back and I was studying at the Eastman School of Music with Bill Street, a percussion teacher there. And I started working at a place called The Pythod which was a local jazz club up there. And they had a lot of people coming through. And Chuck and Gap were local musicians and I think Chuck had the band. He was leading one of the local bands and working in this club. So I think shortly after I got…
Didn’t he always invite the visiting musicians to Rochester over to his house?
